It was the first flight of its kind in 11+ years, flouting the Gulf Coalition’s near-total blockade of Yemeni airspace, imposed in March 2015 during the Saudi-led campaign to try to topple the then newly-formed Houthi-led government.

Reactions

🔴 Friday’s flight sparked panic from the Coalition-backed Yemeni puppet government, which dubbed it a “flagrant violation of national sovereignty” and demanded “concrete deterrent measures” from the UNSC, including new sanctions.

🔴 Yemen’s Houthi-aligned military revealed Saudi jets had tried to intercept the Iranian aircraft, and warned that Riyadh would face a kinetic response on its own territory if further attempts to enforce the blockade were made.

🔴 A Coalition spox threatened to hit the Houthis “with full force and unprecedented strength” if fighting resumed.

🔴 Israeli media did its best to stir the pot. Ynet dubbed the flight a “Saudi surrender in Yemen” and a “catastrophic strategic failure” for Israel – handing Iran “a direct air bridge to the southern border.”

Strategic implications

➡️ The inaugural Sanaa flight is basically Iran flexing its post-war diplomatic muscle - showing that any normalization with Riyadh will be on Tehran's terms

➡️ The Houthis win new legitimacy and opportunities for a civil war peace deal on better terms

➡️ With US regional power currently looking about as intimidating as a wet paper towel, the Gulf States - Saudi Arabia included - are being forced to rethink their entire security playbook, pivoting toward strategic autonomy and de-escalation with Iran

➡️ Regular flights to Sanaa are also a shiny new tool for Iran to project power into Arabia—and strengthen the Houthis' control over Bab al-Mandab.

➡️ Israel, which has been trying to box the Houthis into a corner via everything from US naval missions to a cozy Somaliland partnership, will face increased costs - from shipping to military action - if they try any new aggression against Yemen, which now has a direct air bridge to Tehran

Der Durbin Amendment, ein Bestandteil des Dodd-Frank Acts, begrenzt die Gebühren, die große Banken Händlern für Debitkartentransaktionen über externe Netzwerke berechnen. Besitzt die Bank jedoch das Netzwerk selbst, ist sie von dieser Begrenzung ausgenommen, was laut der Zeitung das Interesse an Fiserv geweckt hat.

Gleichzeitig sind die Aktien von Fiserv im Vergleich zum Vorjahr um etwa 70 % gefallen, was das Unternehmen zu einem potenziellen Übernahmeziel macht.

Matt Ehret lays out a climate argument that moves far beyond the usual carbon-only debate. The clip centers on cosmic radiation, solar activity, cloud formation, the ionosphere, and the possibility that Earth's climate is shaped by forces coming from outside the closed system most people are taught to imagine. Instead of treating weather and climate as a simple machine controlled by one variable, Ehret points to the Sun, the Van Allen belt, solar flares, nearby star systems, and the wider cosmic environment around the planet.

The key figure in this discussion is Henrik Svensmark, the Danish physicist behind The Cloud Mystery. Ehret describes Svensmark's work as a serious challenge to the mainstream climate frame because it connects cosmic rays to cloud formation, which then affects how much heat gets trapped or reflected. Danny pushes him on the evidence and asks for clearer graphs, which makes the exchange sharper than a one-way lecture. The clip becomes a debate about what kind of data is allowed to count when a scientific question has already become political. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zFp-iOFfdqM
